notes: intelligent-routing silently classifies a request (type, domains, complexity) and routes it to the best skill/agent, asking one focused clarifying question when the request is vague. Frontmatter has user-invocable:false, so it is model-invoked only (no slash command); positive prompts as user requests are correct and invocation is automatic. Evaluate whether it picks the correct target, states the routing concisely, and honors explicit user overrides.

evals.prompt: I don't really know where to start with my project — can you help?
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as vague/UNCLEAR and asks ONE focused clarifying question (e.g. implement a new feature vs fix a bug vs review existing code) before routing. Does not spawn work or pick a skill blindly.

evals.prompt: Add product search to the app and make sure it's covered by tests.
evals.expected_output: Detects a multi-domain task (implementation + testing), routes to the orchestrator / parallel agents (developer-agent + unit-test-agent), and states the routing briefly (e.g. 'Routing to: orchestrate — detected implementation + testing').

evals.prompt: Use the fix-bug skill for this checkout crash.
evals.expected_output: Explicit override: the user named a skill, so auto-routing is bypassed and fix-bug is invoked directly regardless of analysis. intelligent-routing should NOT re-route the task elsewhere (matches the Explicit Override edge case).
